prompt: The current capped exponential-backoff delay is 400 milliseconds. Full jitter samples the whole delay interval; equal jitter keeps half certain. Which pair of delay intervals is correct?

options.explanation: Correct. Full jitter samples from zero to the current delay. Equal jitter adds a fixed half-delay to a uniform sample of the other half.
These reverse the distributions: the fixed half-delay belongs to equal jitter.
That describes deterministic backoff with no jitter and preserves synchronised waves.
Full jitter uses the whole current interval, not only its first half; equal jitter does not double the current delay.

workedExample: Full jitter uses the whole interval from zero to the supplied 400-millisecond delay. Equal jitter reserves the first half and randomises the second, so it cannot choose less than 200 milliseconds. Neither distribution proves the dependency has recovered; safety, deadline and retry quota still apply.
